title: 07. Concurrency: Best Practices Cheatsheet
summary: Best Practices Cheatsheet: explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║               ASYNC PYTHON — BEST PRACTICES                         ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  ✅ DO:                                                              ║
║  • Always await coroutines                                           ║
║  • Re-raise CancelledError after cleanup                             ║
║  • Keep references to created tasks                                  ║
║  • Use asyncio.run() once at top level                               ║
║  • Use async with for resource management                            ║
║  • Use asyncio.Semaphore for concurrency limits                      ║
║  • Use asyncio.Queue for producer-consumer                           ║
║  • Name your tasks: create_task(coro(), name="...")                  ║
║  • Use return_exceptions=True in gather() for resilience             ║
║  • Use run_in_executor() for blocking sync code                      ║
║  • Set timeouts on ALL external calls                                ║
║  • Use asyncio debug mode in development                             ║
║  • Use TaskGroup (3.11+) for structured concurrency                  ║
║  • Use contextvars for async-local storage                           ║
║                                                                      ║
║  ❌ DON'T:                                                           ║
║  • Call time.sleep() in async functions                              ║
║  • Use requests.get() in async functions                             ║
║  • Call asyncio.run() inside a running loop                          ║
║  • Suppress CancelledError without re-raising                        ║
║  • Create tasks without keeping references                           ║
║  • Use threading.Lock in async code (use asyncio.Lock)               ║
║  • Block the event loop with CPU-heavy code                          ║
║  • Use bare 'except:' that catches CancelledError                    ║
║  • Forget to close sessions, connections, and files                  ║
║  • Create 10,000 tasks at once without rate limiting                 ║
║  • Mix sync and async I/O without run_in_executor                    ║
║  • Use global mutable state without asyncio.Lock                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```
